court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Family Court, Bandra and Family Court, Nagpur
case_name: Sau. Neekita @ Nishmita W/O Timmy Viadya vs Timmy S/O. Bhardwaj Vaidya

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Sau. Neekita @ Nishmita W/O Timmy Viadya (Applicant-wife)

facts_of_case: Parties got married on 5/11/2017. Applicant-wife initiated proceedings for restitution of conjugal rights pending on the file of Family Court, Bandra. Non-applicant/husband initiated proceedings for divorce under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act which is pending on the file of Family Court, Nagpur.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking transfer of proceedings to establish hardship.
legal_principles.held: Since the contentions are not controverted, it is settled law that the burden lies on the party seeking transfer of proceedings to establish hardship.

legal_principles.principle: A party's choice not to attend proceedings does not justify transfer of the same.
legal_principles.held: I am informed that non-applicant/husband has chosen not to attend the proceedings at Mumbai. However, this court holds that a party's choice not to attend proceedings does not justify transfer of the same.

outcome.final_order: Application is allowed in terms of prayer clause (a).

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
use_for_drafting: drafting divorce petition under Hindu Marriage Act
advising on transfer of family court proceedings
assisting with restitution of conjugal rights
